title: Apple’s 2027 anniversary iPhone 20 rumors, specs and release date
content:
Macworld





The original iPhone was previewed in January 2007 and then released on June 29, 2007. So in 2027, it will turn 20 years old, and rumors point to Apple commemorating the event with a special 20th-anniversary model.
It’s not expected to launch on June 29 (it will probably be in September, as usual), and it may not be a special one-off product, but rather the next major evolution of the iPhone, much like the iPhone X in 2017. But either way, the big two-oh is supposed to bring something really special.
Will Apple call its next-generation models iPhone 19, or skip straight to iPhone 20 to mark the anniversary? Reports suggest the latter is possible, but the name remains unconfirmed. 
Here’s what we’ve gleaned from the rumors and leaks so far.
20th Anniversary iPhone: What to expect
Name: Unconfirmed; one report suggests Apple could skip iPhone 19 and use iPhone 20.
Major redesign: Apple is expected to mark the iPhone’s 20th anniversary in 2027 with a near-all-screen design, curved glass, ultra-thin bezels, and two Pro-sized models.
Display upgrades: Face ID could move under the display, leaving only a small punch-hole front camera for a cleaner look.
Key hardware improvements: Rumored upgrades include a new Sony camera sensor, solid-state haptic buttons, and a silicon-anode battery for better battery life.
More powerful internals: The phone is expected to feature a next generation chip; a C3 modem, and improved wireless connectivity for better performance and efficiency.
Timing and price: A fall 2027 launch is expected with a price of $1,299 or more.


Will Apple skip iPhone 19 and launch iPhone 20?

				
					

				
			
Steve Jobs demonstrating  the first iPhone in January 2007.

Apple




The iPhone that launches in 2027 will mark twenty years since the first iPhone was announced. What will this 20th-anniversary iPhone be called? iPhone 20 is one reported possibility, while iPhone XX remains a speculative alternative.
In October 2025, research firm Omdia reportedly predicted that Apple would skip the iPhone 19 name and move directly to iPhone 20. 
There is a precedent. For the iPhone’s tenth anniversary in 2017, Apple introduced the iPhone 8 and iPhone 8 Plus alongside the iPhone X, skipping iPhone 9 entirely. The iPhone X brought an OLED display with no Home button, Face ID, and a then-record starting price of $999. It also supported wireless charging, which debuted on the iPhone 8 models that year.
Apple could take a similar approach in 2027, launching a standard iPhone 19 alongside a more expensive anniversary model called iPhone 20 – or another name entirely. The 2017 launch shows that Apple can depart from its numbering sequence, but neither the anniversary model’s name nor the possibility of an iPhone 19 launching alongside it is confirmed.


						

							


iPhone 19 or 20 release date: When will the 20th Anniversary iPhone launch?
Likely release date: September 2027
There has been no hard information on the 20th Anniversary iPhone’s release date yet, but it is generally expected to launch in the typical time frame for iPhones: an announcement in September and an on-sale in late September or October 2027.
An August 2026 report from a financial analyst at Jefferies claimed that Apple had canceled the all-glass anniversary iPhone because of manufacturing difficulties and concerns about its financial viability. However, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman disputed that report, saying Apple was still planning a glass-centric redesign for 2027, albeit with changes to its construction.


						

							


How much will the 20th Anniversary iPhone cost?
High starting price estimated at $1,299 or more
It’s too early to predict what the RAM crunch will do to next year’s prices, but we expect the 20th Anniversary iPhone to be expensive. With more advanced technology than most “Pro” iPhones, the starting price will likely be at least $1,299, if not more.


						

							


What will the 20th Anniversary iPhone look like?
Two sizes with slightly larger displays rumored
Edge-to-edge displays
Curved glass design
One of the defining visual characteristics of the 20th Anniversary iPhone will reportedly be its all-display look. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claimed in May 2025 that Apple is planning an all-glass design.  Leaks have described the handset as having “a quad-curved screen design,” with the idea being that the phone will appear to be one big display. Bezels could be minimized to the point where you don’t even see them, and the glass will curve down on all four sides. It’s been reported that Apple could adopt its Liquid Glass branding as well.
“Glass-centric” doesn’t necessarily mean an entirely glass enclosure. According to Gurman’s August 2026 report, Apple encountered difficulties joining the front and back glass panels when preparing the design for mass production. The revised approach reportedly uses a metal band to connect them, while retaining glass that curves around all four sides.
A prominent leaker by the name of Ice Universe on Weibo says Apple is testing two designs, with two sizes for each. One design has a flat back, the other has a curved-glass back. Apple has been refining the curve of that model over time, but it’s not clear which one will go into production.
Reports also suggest that Apple is preparing two anniversary models with slightly larger displays than the current Pro iPhones. According to leaker Digital Chat Station in July 2026, Apple is testing a 6.41-inch display with a resolution of approximately 2,686 × 1,236 pixels and a 6.96-inch display with approximately 2,912 × 1,340 pixels. The larger model could be marketed as having a 7-inch screen, potentially making it the largest display on a conventional, non-folding iPhone.


						

							


Will the 20th Anniversary iPhone have a Dynamic Island?
Under-display Face ID expected
Hole-punch camera for selfie cam rumored

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




One of the persistent rumors over the past several years is that Apple will continue to put more front camera system components under the display, until it’s all display with no cutouts at all.
That may be several years away, but at least some of the components might be able to go behind the OLED display. One rumor claims that Apple will use a “spliced micro-transparent glass,” which will allow it to put the IR emitter under the display, leaving just the regular camera and maybe the IR receiving camera in a cutout region. If the IR camera can effectively go under the display as well, the 20th Anniversary iPhone will have just a single round punch-hole camera in front but retain Face ID.
The Digital Chat Station leak from July 2026 also indicated that Apple is testing a smaller Dynamic Island-style hole-punch design. 
Analyst Ross Young suggested in a post on X back in January 2026 that a smaller Dynamic Island would remain through 2027. He believes Apple’s 2028 iPhone Pro models will feature a centered hole-punch cutout in the display.


						

							


What camera will the 20th Anniversary iPhone have?
Custom LOFIC image sensor rumored
Triple-camera array with telephoto lens

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




According to a Korean-language blog post by a leaker who goes by yeux1122 (who has been accurate in the past with some supply-chain scoops), Apple is working together with Sony on a custom image sensor that uses LOFIC (Lateral Integral Overflow Capacitor) technology.
Phone makers Honor, Xiaomi, and Huawei all use sensors with LOFIC technology in their flagship phones now. It’s a technique that allows sensors to capture low-light or dark areas of an image with less noise, along with brighter areas of an image, without increasing ISO sensitivity. In other words, it gives the camera more dynamic range with less noise.
Otherwise, we expect the 20th Anniversary iPhone to have a triple-camera system like the current Pro models, with wide, ultrawide, and telephoto cameras. It’s likely that the cameras will have significant upgrades, however, with a possible 200MP sensor.


						

							


Will the 20th Anniversary iPhone have physical buttons?
Solid-state with haptics could replace physical buttons

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




On all current MacBooks (other than MacBook Neo), the trackpad doesn’t actually move. Instead, it produces the sensation of being clicked using precise haptic feedback. It’s very effective and reduces the possibility of breakage due to fewer moving parts.
The 20th Anniversary iPhone is supposed to replace the power, volume, Action, and Camera Control buttons with parts that operate in a similar way. These buttons wouldn’t move at all. Rather, they will be integrated into the frame itself, but will have touch capacitors and haptics to give them the feel of an actual button.
Weibo account Instant Digital (with a mixed track record) says extensive testing is ongoing to make sure these new solid-state haptic buttons work well with gloves, cases, wet hands, and so on. 
If Apple can pull this off and they feel as good as real buttons, it will be an important part of the durability of the new iPhone. With the display glass curving down on all edges, the edge area of the frame itself will be very thin, and further cutouts to accommodate buttons would make it less likely to resist bending.


						

							


What specs will the 20th Anniversary iPhone 19 or 20 have?
A next-generation A-series processor is expected
A C3 modem has been rumored
RAM capacity remains unconfirmed
The 20th-anniversary iPhone is expected to feature a successor to the iPhone 18 Pro’s A20 Pro processor, potentially called A21 Pro. Apple has not announced the chip or its specifications.
Reports have suggested that Apple’s C3 cellular modem could arrive in 2027. The C2 is already used in the iPhone 18 Pro worldwide and in the iPhone 18 Pro Max outside the U.S.; the U.S. Pro Max uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80. Whether C3 will appear in every anniversary model remains unconfirmed.
Apple’s N1 wireless chip supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. It is too early to say whether the anniversary iPhone will retain N1 or introduce a successor.
RAM capacity is also unknown. Based on the iPhone 18 Pro, we would expect at least 12GB, while 16GB is a possibility if future features require more memory. This is our assessment rather than a confirmed specification or a sourced claim of a RAM increase.


						

							


Will the 20th Anniversary iPhone have longer battery life?
New battery technology
A report from ETNews in 2025 said that Apple is looking to use a battery with a pure silicon anode in the 20th Anniversary iPhone.
A silicon anode could increase energy density, allowing Apple to fit more battery capacity into the same space or use a smaller battery without sacrificing capacity. Some Android phones already demonstrate the potential of silicon-based batteries: the Oppo Find X9 Pro, for example, has a 7,500mAh silicon-carbon battery. That is different from the pure-silicon anode technology reportedly being considered for Apple’s anniversary iPhone. Apple’s battery capacity remains unknown, and any improvement in battery life would also depend on the display, processor, modem, and software.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 drops to its best price yet ahead of Black Friday
content:
Macworld





		
Apple Watch 12
View Deal
The Apple Watch Series 12 has been out for a couple of months, and the best discount we’ve seen lately has been $10 or $20. Ahead of Black Friday, Apple’s newest smartwatch dropped to $329, a savings of $70 off its MSRP. That’s the best price we’ve ever seen, even lower than the $50 savings during the fall Prime Day, so now’s your chance to get your hands on this product.
The Apple Series 12 comes with a ton of sensors that will come in handy in your day-to-day activity. The heart sensor will read your heart rate every five seconds, which is far more frequently than previous models. Mix that in with your sleep score and activity, and you get a score every day so you know how much energy you have to tackle the day. Battery life on this smartwatch is great too. Apple claims 24 hours on a single charge, but we actually found it delivered a much better performance. In our tests, we used the Series 12 for 45.5 hours before it needed a recharge, which is impressive, but a bit below the 47.5 hours the Series 11 delivered.
You’ll get a few exclusive features with this newest model as well. There are the new Audio Intelligence features, including Siri Recap and Live Rewind, that provide summaries of conversations, the new Health app and Readiness score; as well as faster Siri AI thanks to the new S11 chip. It’s truly a fantastic smartwatch, whether you’re new to Apple Watch or upgrading from an earlier model.
Don’t miss out on this early Black Friday deal for the Apple Watch Series 12 and grab the smartwatch for $70 off while this discount is still live.

Apple also added royalty-free video clips to the Content Hub and a feature for quickly adjusting images in Pixelmator Pro and saving the edits in Final Cut Pro automatically.

Logic Pro has an updated Stem Splitter with the option to break the drum stem into individual tracks, a Liquid Glass design, and Quick Look for previewing audio snapshots.

Sidecar support for turning the iPad into a multi-touch controller, while Motion can use MotionVFX for color grading, 3D camera tracking, and visual effects. Compressor gains support for encoding videos recorded in Cinematic mode.

Pixelmator Pro includes Generate Fill for images, taking advantage of AI for edits that blend in with surrounding content. Apple says the app can match lighting, perspective, and texture. There is a tool to circle an area to edit and improved precision for Magnetic Selection, Free Selection, and Quick Selection.

Pages, Keynote, and Numbers include an Intelligent Assistant that can create and edit content and give guidance on using in-app tools.

title: Apple has a handy new menu bar icon in macOS 27.3. Here’s what it does
content:
Macworld





On Monday, Apple released a note to developers covering the updates to Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access in the upcoming macOS 27.3. In addtion to providing a new user interface for configuring FDA, users will notice another new related feature that’s up in the macOS menu bar.
The developer note states that macOS 27.3 will have, “a transparency indicator when a requesting app is controlling another app using System & App Protection Override.” That indicator comes in the form of a blue icon that looks like a stack behind a cursor. When you click on it, a pop-up menu lists the apps with permissions for System & App Protection Override. On X, arinwaichulis posted screenshots of how it looks.


Another interesting detail in macOS 27.3 beta 2 is this new stack icon
If you give any app full disk access it's PERMANENTLY displayed in the menu bar and updates you on everything it's accessed pic.twitter.com/embqGmvTly
— Arin (@arinwaichulis) November 17, 2026





While arinwaichulis states that the feature lists FDA apps, FDA is different from System & App Protection Override, which is a state where an app controls other apps and can bypass system protections. FDA allows apps to read, change, delete, and export data on your Mac. It’s a nuanced difference, but an app could fall in one category and not necessarily the other. Based on what the developer note said, it’s likely that this is a list of apps granted System & App Protection Override permissions.
The indicator appears in the menu bar by default in the macOS 27.3 beta 2. There currently is no way in System Settings to turn it off and have it not appear, but 9to5Mac posted a way to do it through Terminal commands. In Terminal, enter the following (enter your password when prompted):
sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain
sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false
To restore the indicator, use the following Terminal command: sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false and restart the Mac.
We’re expecting macOS 27.3 to wrap up beta testing and releae in early to mid-December.

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 18, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November.
Black Friday is one of the best opportunities to save on a Mac, with retailers competing to discount MacBooks and desktop models – including recently released machines. Last year, U.S. shoppers could get a 13-inch M4 MacBook Air for $749, saving $250, while the then-new 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro fell to $1,349, also $250 off. Selected M4 Max MacBook Pro configurations received $500 discounts. While U.K. highlights included £150 off the entry-level M4 MacBook Air and savings of around £350 on selected MacBook Pro models.
This year’s deals need a different perspective because Apple raised Mac prices in June. The MacBook Air went up by $200/£200, while some MacBook Pro configurations increased by as much as $500/£500. October Prime Day helped offset those increases: the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB storage fell to $1,099, saving $200, while selected high-end MacBook Pros received discounts of up to $600. Desktop offers included around $120 off the entry-level M6 Mac mini and $200 off the M5 Max Mac Studio.
Those increases mean we may not see a return to earlier record-low prices this Black Friday, even when retailers offer substantial discounts. However, November’s sales could still bring some of the best prices available under Apple’s higher pricing, making this a worthwhile time to buy if you need a new Mac. We’re comparing current offers with previous selling prices and equivalent configurations – not simply the biggest advertised saving – to help you identify genuine value. Below, you’ll find our picks across MacBooks and desktop Macs; for discounts on Apple’s other products, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Which Mac or MacBook should you buy this Black Friday?


MacBook Air – Our best overall choice 

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




The MacBook Air is our recommendation for most buyers. Both sizes offer a lightweight, silent laptop for everyday work, studying, and occasional creative projects. Choose the 13-inch for portability or the 15-inch for more workspace without MacBook Pro pricing.
We’d prioritize a competitive price on the memory and storage you need. For regular lengthy exports or other sustained demanding tasks, consider a MacBook Pro with active cooling instead.
U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the 13-inch M5 Air with 16GB memory and 512GB storage to $1,099, and the equivalent 15-inch to $1,299. Last Black Friday, the older M4 models with 256GB reached $749 and $949 respectively. We are already seeing up to $250 off the 1TB models, and $200 off the 512GB options, bringing the price back to the original MSRP before Apple increased prices.  
U.K. Black Friday price: October offers included approximately £1,199 for the 13-inch M5 Air and £1,349 for the 15-inch, both with 512GB storage. Last Black Friday’s M4 models with 256GB reached £849 and £1,025. Match storage capacities when comparing generations. So far in November 2026, we have seen £200 off the 13-inch MacBook Air and £200 off the 15-inch model, which are better than what we saw for Prime Day this October. Now the savings have dropped to a maximum £150 off though.


						

							


MacBook Neo – Our budget choice, at the right price

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




The MacBook Neo suits browsing, schoolwork, streaming, and office apps. Its lower starting price makes it appealing, but its fixed 8GB of memory leaves less room for demanding workloads.
Check which configuration is discounted: only the 512GB version includes Touch ID. Both lack a backlit keyboard, MagSafe, and Thunderbolt. Compare clearance MacBook Air stock before deciding how much those compromises save you.
U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has cut the price of the both Neo models by $50, the best discount we’ve seen so far. Previously the Neo was only ever discounted by $10-$15.
U.K. Black Friday price: We saw a Prime Day low of £549, but that was before Apple increased prices. Now the low is £649, £50 off for the 256GB model. We are also seeing £79 off the 512GB MacBook Neo. 


						

							


MacBook Pro M6 – Best step up from the Air

				
					

				
			
Macbook Pro M6 Aufmacher

Halyna Kubiv




The standard M6 MacBook Pro is worth considering if you want a better built-in display, more connections, and cooling for sustained workloads without paying for a Pro or Max chip. It comes in a 14-inch size, with a non-touch Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI, and an SDXC card slot.
It starts with 16GB memory and 1TB storage, so account for those specifications when comparing prices with an Air or older Pro. Despite the newer generation number, the standard M6 isn’t automatically the better choice for demanding work than an M5 Pro or M5 Max.
U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 model wasn’t available during October Prime Day. Its M5 predecessor with 16GB memory and 1TB storage reached $1,839. We aren’t seeing discounts on the M6 yet, but you can get the 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro for $200 less than the new model.
U.K. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the older 14-inch M5 with 16GB memory and 1TB storage reached approximately £1,619. We are already seeing £169 off the 14-inch, M6 with 1TB, 16GB, also note that it is only £31.97 more than the M5 (£1,830.97 versus £1,799), so we wouldn’t recommend the older model. 


						

							


MacBook Pro M5 Pro – Best for demanding professional work

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The non-touchscreen M5 Pro MacBook Pro is a strong choice for development, photography, video editing, and heavier multitasking. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, it offers professional performance without the Max chip’s higher price.
Compare it with the touchscreen version using the same memory and storage. Both offer M5 Pro configurations, so a discounted non-touch model could be particularly good value if its existing XDR display meets your needs.
U.S. Black Friday price: October prices included $2,339 for the 14-inch M5 Pro with 24GB memory and 1TB storage, and $2,749 for the equivalent 16-inch. So far this Black Friday month we are seeing $250 off the 16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro, 1TB).
U.K. Black Friday price: The equivalent configurations reached approximately £2,250 and £2,700. Last Black Friday, selected previous-generation M4 Pro models received discounts of around £350. So far this Black Friday there is a £349 saving on the 16-inch M5 Pro model. Note that the 14-inch M5 Pro, 2TB/24GB model is only £24.03 more than the 1TB/24GB version.


						

							


MacBook Pro M5 Max – Best for demanding graphics and video

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




Consider the non-touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro if your work benefits from additional graphics power or more memory than an M5 Pro supports. Complex 3D projects and demanding video production make a stronger case for it than everyday productivity.
We’d choose the configuration around the work you do. A larger advertised discount on a Max doesn’t necessarily make it better value than a less expensive Pro that meets your needs. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the options.
U.S. Black Friday price:  October offers included $3,499 for a 14-inch M5 Max with 2TB storage and $3,899 for a 16-inch with 36GB memory and 2TB storage. Last Black Friday, selected M4 Max configurations were $500 off and this Black Friday month we are already seeing $500 off the M5 Max models. 
U.K. Black Friday price:  October coverage included a 14-inch M5 Max with 2TB storage at £3,799, saving £300. This time there is £100 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 Max.


						

							


Touchscreen MacBook Pro – Best for its OLED display

				
					

				
			


Roman Loyola/Foundry




The touchscreen MacBook Pro is most compelling for its OLED display and thinner, lighter design. Improved blacks and reduced blooming could matter more to your everyday experience than touch controls, particularly if you spend most of your working day using the built-in screen.
Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, these models offer comparable processing performance to their non-touch equivalents. Compare matching configurations: the regular premium is $400/£400, so consider how much you’ll benefit from the display before paying extra.
U.S. Black Friday price:  These models arrived in November, so there are no equivalent October Prime Day or Black Friday 2025 prices. Compare any offer with the matching non-touch M5 Pro or M5 Max model. It’s early days so we don’t expect to see big savings here this Black Friday. 
U.K. Black Friday price: In the U.K. we have seen Amazon knock £286 off the price of the MacBook Pro (16-inch, M5 Pro, 1TB, Touchscreen), which helps with affordability for what is a very expensive machine. 


						

							


Mac mini M6 – Our best-value desktop choice

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The M6 Mac mini suits buyers who already own a display, keyboard, and mouse. It offers a compact desktop for everyday work and lighter creative projects. Check storage carefully: the entry-level model has a restrictive 256GB SSD.
U.S. Black Friday price: October’s entry-level M6 mini reached approximately $780. Last Black Friday, the older M4 equivalent was $479. So far this November we’ve seen $150 off the 512GB model.
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s M6 model reached approximately £824, compared with £499 for the M4 last Black Friday. There’s £100 off the 256GB Mac mini in the U.K.


						

							


Mac mini M5 Pro – Best compact desktop for professional work

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




The M5 Pro mini offers more processing power and memory capacity for demanding work without moving to a Studio. Compare upgraded configurations carefully: if the total approaches Mac Studio pricing, check which machine better suits your workload.
U.S. Black Friday price: The 24GB/512GB M5 Pro mini reached approximately $1,550 in October. Last Black Friday’s M4 Pro equivalent was $1,249. So far this November we’ve seen $150 off the 512GB model.
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s M5 Pro configuration reached approximately £1,647. The previous-generation M4 Pro with 24GB/512GB was £1,269 last Black Friday. There is £150 off the 512GB Mac mini M5 Pro in the U.K. 


						

							


iMac – Best complete desktop setup

				
					

				
			

Foundry




The iMac combines a 24-inch 4.5K display with the computer and matching accessories. Compare the two-port and four-port versions carefully: the latter adds processing power, connections, and a Touch ID keyboard. Factor those differences into the final price.
U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 wasn’t available during October Prime Day. The entry-level M4 predecessor reached approximately $1,360 in October and $1,149 last Black Friday. We’ve not seen any savings yet. 
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s four-port M4 with 256GB storage was £1,620. Last Black Friday, comparable four-port M4 stock reached £1,349. These are predecessor prices rather than M6 targets. The new iMac models aren’t discounted at the moment. 


						

							


Mac Studio – Best for demanding desktop workflows

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




The M5 Max Studio suits demanding graphics, video, and other professional workloads. Compare it with the M5 Pro mini first. The considerably more expensive M5 Ultra is for exceptional workloads requiring its additional performance and memory; most buyers won’t need it. Budget for a display and peripherals.
U.S. Black Friday price: October’s M5 Max Studio with 36GB memory and 512GB storage reached approximately $2,300. There’s currently a $200 saving, which is the same as October’s $200 discount.

Should you buy a Mac or MacBook now or wait for a better deal?
With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need a Mac immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so an early offer can be worth taking if it matches or approaches a previous low for the same configuration. Waiting can be a gamble if you’re buying clearance stock with a particular screen size, memory capacity, or finish.
The M5 MacBook Air remains an appealing purchase at a good discount, with a replacement not expected until 2027. The recently updated Mac mini and Mac Studio are also worth considering if they meet your needs. The main reason to wait is a better price rather than an imminent replacement.
MacBook Pro buyers no longer need to wait for the rumored October launches: the standard M6 and OLED touchscreen models are now available. However, their recent arrival may limit initial discounts. Non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max models could offer better value, particularly if you don’t need the touchscreen version’s improved display and lighter design. If your existing M4 or M5 MacBook Pro still meets your needs, there’s little reason to upgrade simply because a newer option exists.
The M6 iMac has only just arrived, replacing the aging M4 version. Compare a modest saving on the latest model with a substantial clearance discount on its predecessor, rather than assuming the older machine is automatically the better deal.
Previous prices need context this year. Following June’s increases, a discount from Apple’s current asking price may still leave you paying more than before the increases. Compare retailers as well: Amazon competes with Best Buy, Walmart, and B&H in the U.S., and retailers including Currys and John Lewis in the U.K. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the current choices.


						

							


Which Mac specifications are worth paying for?
The cheapest Mac isn’t always the best value. Use Black Friday to get a configuration that will serve you for longer within your budget, but don’t pay for performance or features you won’t use.
Check the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. A standard M6 and an M5 Pro or M5 Max serve different needs: the newer generation number alone doesn’t tell you which is better for your work. For MacBook Pro listings, distinguish the OLED touchscreen version from non-touch models.
Avoid saving a small amount by buying too little memory or storage. Most current Macs start with 16GB of unified memory, but the MacBook Neo has a fixed 8GB, and some desktop configurations include only a 256GB SSD. Unified memory cannot be upgraded later. An external SSD can add storage, but it cannot compensate for insufficient RAM.
Once the processor meets your needs, additional memory may be more useful than a faster chip. Compare a discounted Air with the Neo, too: the M5 Air starts with twice the memory and storage of the entry-level Neo. Our Mac buying guide explains which specifications suit different workloads.
Check whether the configuration includes nano-texture glass. This optional finish reduces glare and reflections, which can help in bright rooms or near windows, but increases the price. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may offer better value.


						

							


Should you buy an older Mac or MacBook?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older Mac can be excellent value if its price reflects its age and configuration. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of the newer equivalent, rather than focusing on a large percentage saving from its original launch price.
Previous-generation Apple silicon models are the most promising starting point. A discounted M4 MacBook Air or standard M5 MacBook Pro may meet your needs comfortably. Older Pro and Max configurations can also be worth considering if they provide the memory, graphics performance, and connections your work requires for substantially less money.
Check what the saving buys—and what you give up. An older Mac with more memory or storage could be more useful than a newer entry-level configuration. Conversely, a cheaper older Air with 256GB storage isn’t directly comparable with an M5 Air that starts with 512GB. The non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros also remain current options, despite the arrival of the standard M6 and touchscreen models.
Be much more cautious with Intel Macs. Their software support is winding down, and a low purchase price may leave you with a machine that has a limited useful life for current apps and macOS features. Check compatibility with the software you need before buying any older model.
For used or refurbished Macs, check battery condition on laptops, warranty coverage, and the returns policy. Confirm that Activation Lock has been removed and that the Mac isn’t still enrolled in an organization’s management system.
For more advice read:
Should I buy a MacBook Neo?
Should I buy a MacBook Air?
Should I buy a MacBook Pro?
Should I buy a Mac mini?
Should I buy a Mac Studio?


						

							


Mac or MacBook deals to avoid
Treat large advertised discounts carefully. Following June’s price increases, “$400 off” may simply bring a Mac closer to what it cost before the increase. Compare previous selling prices for the same configuration, rather than judging the offer solely against today’s recommended price.
Check whether the price includes AppleCare+ or another protection plan. Some Amazon listings bundle coverage with the Mac. If you don’t want it, a listing without coverage could be cheaper; if you do, compare the bundle with buying the Mac and coverage separately.
Check for a bundled power adapter, too. Some Mac laptops are sold without one in the U.K. and EU. A charger bundle may be useful if you need an adapter, but could mean paying extra unnecessarily if you already own a suitable one.
Compare the complete setup cost. A Mac mini or Studio requires a display, keyboard, and mouse or trackpad, while adapters and docks can add to the cost of any Mac.
Finally, distinguish cash discounts from gift cards, trade-ins, financing, and membership-only offers. Read the conditions, check the seller, and confirm whether the Mac is new, refurbished, or used, along with its warranty and returns policy.


						

							


How we choose Mac and MacBook deals
Macworld has covered the Mac since its launch in 1984, and our recommendations draw on decades of experience and hands-on reviews. We consider performance, display quality, battery life, portability, connectivity, and everyday use alongside price to explain which Macs suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess which upgrades are worth paying for. We look at whether additional processing power benefits demanding workloads, when more memory is useful, and whether a premium display justifies the extra cost. A MacBook Air may offer better value for everyday work, while a Pro, Max, or Ultra configuration needs to earn its higher price through the work it enables.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than judging a deal solely against today’s recommended retail price. A large advertised discount doesn’t automatically make an offer exceptional.
We consider the complete purchase, too: the retailer, product condition, warranty, and any conditions attached to the price. For desktop Macs, we also account for the display and accessories you’ll need. Our Mac buying guide and MacBook comparison explain how to choose the right model and configuration.

Black Friday is a great time to buy an Apple Watch, with retailers discounting everything from the affordable SE to the premium Ultra. Last year’s U.S. offers included $50 off the SE 3, up to $70 off the then-new Series 11, and $100 off the Ultra 3. Older models brought bigger savings, including $150 off the Series 10 and $200 off the Ultra 2. In the U.K., clearance offers were particularly attractive: the Series 10 was up to £130 off at Currys, while Argos cut £200 from the Ultra 2’s original price.
October Prime Day brought discounts on this year’s models, too. In the U.S., the 42mm Series 12 fell to $349, the 40mm SE 3 to $199, and the Ultra 4 to $774 – savings of $50, $50, and $25 respectively. U.K. highlights included the SE 3 at £199 and the previous-generation Series 11 at £259.
This Black Friday, we’d look for discounts on the Series 12, our pick as the best Apple Watch for most people, the SE 3 for an affordable entry point, and the Ultra 4 for longer battery life and outdoor features. Remaining Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock could offer particularly good value if priced sufficiently below their replacements. Below, we explain which offers are worth taking and when to wait; for savings across Apple’s other products, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Which Apple Watch should you buy this Black Friday?


Apple Watch Series 12 – Our best overall choice

				
					

				
			

Apple




The Series 12 is the Apple Watch we recommend for most people. It combines Apple’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate measurements, a Readiness score, and a tougher display with up to 24 hours of battery life.
A worthwhile Black Friday discount could make it an attractive purchase, but compare it with remaining Series 11 stock. The older model has the same quoted battery life, so a substantial saving may outweigh the newer health features.
U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has already discounted the 42mm GPS Series 12 to $329, saving  $70 and the best price we’ve ever seen. The 46mm version is also $70 off.
U.K. Black Friday price: We didn’t see Series 12 discounts during October Prime Day, and so far this November there have been no price drops, but we are hopeful. We have only seen discounts on older models so far.


						

							


Apple Watch Ultra 4 – Best for battery life and outdoor adventures

				
					

				
			

Apple




The Ultra 4 is our choice for endurance athletes, outdoor enthusiasts, and buyers who prioritize battery life. It offers up to 50 hours of normal use, satellite communication, precision dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and Apple’s new Health Sensing System.
It’s more watch than most people need. Compare it with the Ultra 3, though, which retains many of its outdoor features but has a shorter 42-hour battery-life rating.
U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the Ultra 4 down to $774, a $25 saving. This November we’ve already seen the Apple Watch Ultra 4 for $699.99 on Amazon: that’s $99 off. However, the price is now up to $774, so we recommend watching for the price to dip again.
U.K. Black Friday price: The Ultra 4 remained at its full £749 price during October Prime Day, but we’ve already seen it drop by £30 to £719 at Amazon.


						

							


Apple Watch SE 3 – Our best budget choice

				
					

				
			
Apple / Amazon




The SE 3 is the best-value option for buyers who want the core Apple Watch experience. It includes an always-on display, temperature sensing, fast charging, and the S10 chip, but lacks ECG, blood oxygen monitoring, and the newer Health Sensing System.
It remains part of Apple’s current lineup despite launching in 2025. A strong Black Friday offer could make it an excellent affordable purchase, although its previous discounts mean there’s little reason to settle for a token reduction.
U.S. Black Friday price: Both last Black Friday and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to $199 and the 44mm version to $229 – $50 below their regular prices. Already, the U.S. price is $199, $50 off at Amazon.
U.K. Black Friday price: Black Friday 2025 and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to £199 and the 44mm version to £229, saving £20. So far we haven’t seen any price drops for Black Friday 2026.


						

							


Apple Watch Ultra 3 – Best clearance option for outdoor enthusiasts

				
					

				
			
Apple




The Ultra 3 is worth considering if you want a rugged Apple Watch without paying for the latest model. It offers satellite communication, dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and up to 42 hours of battery life.
You give up the Ultra 4’s longer battery life and newer Health Sensing System. Compare their actual selling prices: the Ultra 3 needs to be sufficiently cheaper to justify choosing the older generation.
U.S. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the Ultra 3 fell to $699, a $100 saving. Our October Prime Day coverage found only used models, so it didn’t identify a comparable new-stock offer. So far this November we’ve seen the Apple Watch Ultra 3 for $649, but that’s now out of stock.
U.K. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the Ultra 3 was £719, or £30 off. October Prime Day listed it at £569. The price is even lower this November – you can get it for £495 at Amazon, which is £304 less than the usual Apple Watch Ultra 4 price.


						

							


Apple Watch Series 11 – Best clearance option for everyday use

				
					

				
			
Apple Watch Series 11




The Series 11 could be a better-value everyday watch than the Series 12 if the price gap is large enough. It has the same quoted 24-hour battery life, although it lacks the newer Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features.
For buyers who don’t need those additions, a substantial clearance discount could be more useful than a small saving on the latest model.
U.S. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the 42mm GPS Series 11 reached $339, while the 46mm version was $359 – savings of $60 and $70, respectively. Our October Prime Day coverage found only used models in the U.S. and so far that’s all we are seeing this November.

Should you buy an Apple Watch now or wait for a better deal?
With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need an Apple Watch immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so you don’t necessarily need to wait for Black Friday itself. If an early offer matches or comes close to a previous low for the same model and configuration, it can be worth taking – particularly if you want a specific size, color, or band combination.
October Prime Day prices provide useful benchmarks. In the U.S., the Series 12 fell to $349 for the 42mm GPS model and $399 for the 46mm version, while the Ultra 4 reached $774. The SE 3 was $199 in 40mm and $229 in 44mm. Those SE prices also appeared last Black Friday, so we’d look for offers matching or beating them. In the U.K., October highlights included the 40mm SE 3 at £199 and the older 42mm Series 11 at £259.
The Series 12 and Ultra 4 only arrived in September, so finding a better price is the main reason to wait. If you don’t need a watch immediately, those previous offers give you a useful starting point for deciding whether to buy now or hold out.
Compare retailers, too. Last Black Friday, Walmart offered $150 off the Series 10, while U.K. shoppers could find up to £130 off at Currys and £200 off the Ultra 2’s original price at Argos. Our guide to the best time to buy an Apple Watch has more advice on choosing when to purchase.


						

							


Should you buy an older Apple Watch?

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Don’t assume an older Apple Watch is a bad buy. The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are only one generation old and can make excellent purchases if they’re substantially cheaper than the Series 12 or Ultra 4. Both retain many of their replacements’ core features, although you miss the newer Health Sensing System and, with the Ultra 3, the Ultra 4’s longer battery life.
Compare actual selling prices, matching case size, material, connectivity, and band where possible. A $50 difference between a Series 11 and Series 12 may not be enough to justify giving up the newer model’s health features, whereas a substantially larger saving could change the calculation. A discounted Series 11 could also be worth considering alongside the SE 3 if a small premium gets you features you’ll use.
Be much more cautious with the Series 8, SE 2, and original Ultra: those models cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 9 is the oldest standard Apple Watch compatible with the latest software, while the Ultra 2 is the oldest supported Ultra and the SE 3 is the only supported SE. Missing the latest software doesn’t make an older watch unusable, but it makes it harder to recommend as a purchase today.
The Series 9, Series 10, and Ultra 2 can still be worth considering at sufficiently low prices. However, compatibility with today’s software doesn’t guarantee how many future upgrades they’ll receive. Weigh the savings against the watch’s age and features, rather than assuming every supported generation offers equally good value.


						

							


Apple Watch deals to avoid 

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Don’t let a bigger advertised discount tempt you into paying more for a cellular Apple Watch you won’t use. If your iPhone is usually nearby, a GPS model can already handle calls, messages, and notifications through your phone. It can also track runs, use Apple Pay, and play downloaded music without your iPhone. As our experience testing a cellular Apple Watch showed, the extra connectivity may add little to everyday use.
Cellular is worth considering if you regularly leave your iPhone behind and want to remain contactable without Wi-Fi, or you’re setting up a watch for a child without an iPhone. Otherwise, you could pay extra for the hardware and then add an ongoing mobile-plan charge for a feature you rarely need. You don’t have to activate a plan on a cellular model, so it can still be a good buy if its sale price matches or beats the GPS version. Our GPS versus cellular Apple Watch guide explains the trade-offs.
Check the rest of the configuration, too. A premium case material or expensive band can make a heavily discounted watch cost more than a simpler version that meets your needs. Judge offers against previous selling prices as well as the advertised reduction: a large saving from the original launch price doesn’t necessarily mean exceptional value. Check any spending requirements, contracts, trade-ins, or rebates attached to offers advertising a “free” Apple Watch.
Finally, check whether you’re buying a new, refurbished, or used watch, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For a used or refurbished model, check the stated battery condition and confirm that it has been removed from the previous owner’s account, with Activation Lock turned off. Make sure the watch is compatible with your iPhone before ordering.


						

							


How we choose Apple Watch deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on Apple Watch reviews and everyday wear. We consider comfort, performance, battery life, charging, health and fitness features, and value – not just the specifications or advertised saving.
Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our Series 12 review assessed battery life and charging performance alongside its newer health features. We also draw on everyday experience: our cellular Apple Watch testing examines whether staying connected without an iPhone justified the extra hardware and subscription costs.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. We check the generation, case size, material, connectivity, and included band so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside discounted replacements.
Our Best Apple Watch guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the right choice: your budget, wrist size, activities, and the features you need all matter.

title: The new HomePod mini’s boring colors finally make sense to me
content:
Macworld





Yesterday I made a rare trip south of the Thames to visit Apple’s stunning Battersea Power Station headquarters in London, where I was given a chance to try out HomeView (on which I will soon have more to say) as well as the new Apple TV and HomePod mini. And while I was there, one of the product managers helped me to reach a small logical breakthrough.
I spend far too much time thinking about product colors, and was quite loudly critical when the options for the 2nd-gen HomePod mini were unveiled last month. There are still five finishes, and these still include black, white, and very dark blue. But the two nicest from 2021, a rich autumnal orange and a glorious marigold yellow, both of which I promptly bought, have been replaced by dark green and a washed-out pink. This, in my opinion, is displeasing.

				
					

				
			The somber new color options for 2026.Apple
Photography doesn’t always do justice to the color of tech products, and my first thought when wandering around the demo environment was that the new HomePod mini looks nicer in the flesh than I expected. The pink is still paler than I’d like, but it’s fine, and the green is undeniably smart. Even the ostensibly most boring options, black and white and dark blue, work in a real-world context in a way they don’t on a webpage with a white background.
The real revelation, however, came when the product manager showed me a stereo pair of green HomePods which had been set up either side of a green iMac. The new models, he casually mentioned, were color-matched to the company’s famously attractive all-in-one desktop.
Right. Of course.
Now, it’s important to stress that this doesn’t mean the two sets of products are in every case exactly the same shade (although the greens are remarkably close, as you can see above). Nor does it mean that the two ranges line up perfectly; there’s no black iMac, while the HomePod mini range doesn’t have a purple option, and as previously mentioned no longer includes orange and yellow. Essentially what we mean is that the green, blue, and pink HomePods will go nicely with the green, blue, and pink iMacs.

				
					

				
			The HomePod mini’s color options in 2021. (When it launched in 2020, only black and white were available.)
Apple




The point is that, where colors are offered on both products, they have been explicitly and consciously designed to go together harmoniously. This hasn’t always been the case. The bright orange and yellow HomePods, for example, were not (at least in my subjective view) a good match for the orange and yellow iMacs, because they’re different renditions of those colors. The orange HomePod is insufficiently peachy and the yellow HomePod too orangey to work well with their equivalents. And they’re both too bold to suit the softer colors of the iMac.
In other words, while the new colors may not be quite as exciting as the last set, they’re more considered and a lot more co-ordinated. And on this type of tech, that counts.
When you consider a product purely as an object in isolation or on an otherwise blank page, bright colors seem like the way to go. But when you think decoratively, as we must for home tech, it’s sometimes better to go for a safe color which won’t clash with the carpet or the wallpaper. You have to consider the other elements. And even though I remain a fan of bright colors, Apple’s choice to go for duller options this year now makes a lot more sense to me.

October Prime Day brought further discounts, although Apple’s June price increases made the advertised savings less straightforward. In the U.S., the 128GB A16 iPad was $399, the 128GB A17 Pro mini was $499, and the 11-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB was $649. U.K. offers included £80 off the 13-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB. Those prices show why it’s worth checking previous selling prices as well as today’s discount: an offer below Apple’s current asking price may still cost more than the same iPad did earlier in the year.
This Black Friday, we’d watch the M4 iPad Air for a balance of performance and price, the A16 iPad for a worthwhile budget deal, and the M5 iPad Pro for buyers who need its premium capabilities. The new A20 Pro iPad mini, with its OLED display, also changes the calculation: we’d expect smaller initial discounts on the new arrival, while remaining A17 Pro stock could offer clearance bargains. Below, we explain which deals are worth taking, checking the generation, storage, and connectivity rather than simply choosing the biggest advertised saving. For offers across Apple’s other products, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Which iPad should you buy this Black Friday?


M4 iPad Air – Our best all-round choice

				
					

				
			
Apple Inc




The iPad Air offers a strong balance of performance, screen size, and price without the premium cost of the Pro. The 11-inch model suits buyers who prioritize portability, while the 13-inch version gives you more room for multitasking and creative work.
A good Black Friday discount could make either size an attractive purchase. Compare storage capacities carefully, though: a larger advertised saving on a high-capacity model isn’t necessarily better value if you don’t need the extra space.
U.S. Black Friday price: At Amazon, you can already get a saving of $100 off some iPad Air models. Last Black Friday, the 11-inch and 13-inch M3 models were $449 and $649, respectively, which was $150 off the old price, so we hope to see discounts of at least $150 again, although starting prices are now considerably higher.
U.K. Black Friday price: There’s £49 off the 128GB 13-inch iPad Air and £44 off the 256GB 11-inch iPad Air. These are reasonable savings, although we saw better discounts during October Prime Day, with up to £144 off. Last Black Friday, selected M3 Air configurations received £100 discounts.


						

							


iPad Pro – Best for demanding creative work

				
					

				
			
Apple Inc




The iPad Pro is the option for buyers who need Apple’s highest-end tablet performance and premium display. It comes in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes, but its capabilities – and price – will exceed what many people need for browsing, streaming, and everyday apps.
We’d look for a substantial saving rather than buy simply because it’s the most powerful iPad. Compare discounted M4 iPad Pro models, too: an older Pro could offer better value if its price is sufficiently below the equivalent M5 configuration.
U.S. Black Friday price:  During October Prime Day, the 11-inch M5 Pro with 256GB was $1,099, saving $100. So far we’re seeing nearly $300 off a 1TB 11-inch iPad Pro.
U.K. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought little to recommend on the M5 Pro, with reductions of around £12. Last Black Friday, older M4 iPad Pro offers included a saving of approximately £206 at Amazon. Currently, the biggest saving is £150 off the 11-inch, 1TB model.


						

							


iPad (A16) – Our budget choice, at the right price

				
					

				
			
Apple




The A16 iPad remains a capable option for browsing, streaming, schoolwork, and everyday use. However, Apple raised its starting price by $100/£100 in June, and it doesn’t support Apple Intelligence.
That makes the final purchase price particularly important. A modest discount from today’s higher asking price may still leave you paying more than this iPad previously cost. With a replacement expected early in 2027, we’d look for a substantial Black Friday saving and compare the price with discounted iPad Air models before buying.
U.S. Black Friday price: The 128GB A16 iPad was $399 during October Prime Day, saving $50 against its increased $449 price. Last Black Friday, it briefly reached $279. This Black Friday we are already seeing $49 off the 128GB iPad. However, at $399.99, this isn’t an offer we’d rush to buy. It approximately matches October’s $399 price and is well above the $279 we saw last Black Friday. We’d wait for a better discount as Black Friday approaches.
U.K. Black Friday price: October coverage listed the 256GB model at £499.97, around £29 off. Last Black Friday, the 128GB version was £299 and the 256GB version was £399. We hope to see even lower prices this year, but so far the discount is £30 off the iPad.


						

							


iPad mini with A20 Pro – Best for portability

				
					

				
			
Apple




The new iPad mini went on sale on November 6, replacing the A17 Pro model. It brings an 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, and a thinner, lighter design, making it the option to consider if you want a compact iPad with the latest hardware.
Because it has only just arrived, we’d expect initial discounts to be smaller than clearance savings on its predecessor. The older A17 Pro mini could still be worthwhile at a sufficiently low price, but compare the saving with what you give up – particularly the new display.
U.S. Black Friday price: The A20 Pro mini wasn’t available during October Prime Day or last Black Friday. Its 128GB A17 Pro predecessor was $499 during October Prime Day and $399 last Black Friday. Unsurprisingly, there are no discounts on the new models – but you can save around $200 on the price of the A17 Pro iPad mini compared to the newer equivalent. This is the same offer we saw during October Prime Day.
U.K. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought only a small saving on the A17 Pro mini in our coverage. The 128GB version reached £399 earlier this year, though – before Apple pushed up prices. You can still get the A17 Pro iPad mini for £100 less than the new model, but we hope to see bigger savings as Black Friday approaches.

Should you buy an iPad now or wait for a better deal?

				
					

				
			
There’s an iPad for everyone.

Foundry




With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need an iPad immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so an early offer can be worth taking if the price is competitive. Compare the exact generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity rather than waiting for Black Friday simply because a larger discount might appear.
Previous selling prices are particularly important this year because Apple raised iPad prices in June. During October Prime Day, the 128GB A16 iPad was $399, while the 11-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB was $649. Both were discounted against Apple’s increased prices, but cost more than their regular prices before June. A saving from today’s asking price doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting an exceptional bargain.
For the M4 iPad Air and M5 iPad Pro, we’d focus on finding a good price: We don’t expect replacements until 2027, as explained in our guide to the best time to buy an iPad. We’d be more cautious about the A16 iPad, which lacks Apple Intelligence and is expected to be replaced. Unless you find a substantial saving, waiting could get you a more capable entry-level model.
The new A20 Pro iPad mini presents a different decision. It has only just arrived, so we’d expect smaller initial discounts rather than immediate clearance-level savings. If you want its OLED display and newer processor, a modest reduction may still be worthwhile. If price matters more, compare remaining A17 Pro stock – but make sure the saving justifies choosing the older hardware.


						

							


Should you buy an older iPad? 

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older iPad can be a good buy if its price reflects its age and the features you give up. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of its replacement, matching screen size, storage, and connectivity where possible. A large saving from an old launch price doesn’t necessarily make it better value.
The M3 iPad Air and M4 iPad Pro are worth considering at substantial clearance discounts. Both remain capable options, and you may get more benefit from a lower price or additional storage than from the latest processor. However, if the newer equivalent costs only slightly more, the saving may not justify choosing the older generation.
The A17 Pro iPad mini also deserves consideration now that the A20 Pro model has arrived. It supports Apple Intelligence and remains a capable compact tablet, but you miss the newer model’s OLED display, faster processor, and thinner, lighter design. We’d want a meaningful saving rather than a small reduction from its former asking price.
Be more cautious with much older models. Check whether they support the current version of iPadOS and the apps and features you need. Compatibility today doesn’t guarantee how many future software upgrades they’ll receive. Apple Intelligence support also varies: don’t assume every older Air, Pro, or mini includes it.
If you already own an Apple Pencil or keyboard, check compatibility before changing generations. Keeping compatible accessories could make an older iPad better value, while replacing them could erase part of your saving. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges.


						

							


iPad deals to avoid
Check the exact configuration before comparing offers. Retailer listings can emphasize iPad, Air, or Pro without making the generation obvious. Confirm the chip, screen size, storage capacity, and whether you’re buying Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi + Cellular. A cheaper listing may be a different model rather than a better deal.
Don’t let a large advertised discount tempt you into paying for storage or connectivity you won’t use. A heavily reduced high-capacity or cellular iPad can still cost more than a simpler configuration that meets your needs. Compare the final purchase prices, rather than assuming the biggest saving represents the best value.
Check whether the price includes nano-texture glass, too. This optional finish reduces glare and makes fingerprints and oily smudges less noticeable, which can be useful if reflections make your iPad difficult to see in bright rooms or outdoors. It avoids much of the washed-out appearance associated with ordinary matte finishes, but contrast can drop at some viewing angles and the surface may be more scratch-sensitive. Availability depends on the model and storage configuration, so you could end up paying for both the finish and additional storage. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may be better value. Read our guide to nano-texture glass and whether you need it.
Our iPad buying guide considers cellular a luxury for most buyers. If you mainly use your iPad somewhere with Wi-Fi, you may get little benefit from the extra hardware. For occasional use elsewhere, sharing your iPhone’s connection through Personal Hotspot can be a more economical option.
Cellular makes more sense if you regularly need an independent connection while commuting or traveling; it also adds built-in GPS for accurate location tracking. Factor in any data-plan charges and compare the total cost of a contract with buying outright. A cellular model can still be worthwhile if its sale price matches or beats the equivalent Wi-Fi version—you don’t have to activate a data plan simply because the hardware is included.
Judge savings against previous selling prices as well as Apple’s current price. Following June’s price increases, a discounted iPad may still cost more than it did earlier in the year. Also distinguish a cash discount from a gift-card offer: a gift card doesn’t reduce the amount you pay for the iPad and is useful only if you’ll spend it.
Check what any bundle includes. A keyboard, case, or stylus doesn’t automatically make an offer better value, particularly if the accessories aren’t the versions you want. Read the conditions attached to “free” iPads, trade-in promotions, contracts, and rebates before comparing their total cost with buying outright.
Finally, check whether the iPad is new, refurbished, or used, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For used or refurbished models, look for information about battery condition and confirm that Activation Lock has been removed. Be cautious about devices that remain tied to a previous owner or an organization’s management system.


						

							


How we choose iPad deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on iPad reviews and everyday use. We consider performance, display quality, portability, battery life, and accessory support alongside price to explain which iPads suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess whether paying more brings practical benefits. A faster processor or premium display may matter for demanding creative work, while a less expensive iPad can be perfectly capable of browsing, streaming, and schoolwork. We also consider the cost of keyboards, Apple Pencils, and other accessories when judging an iPad’s value.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than relying solely on savings against today’s recommended price.
Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside newer alternatives. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges, while our purchase-timing guide helps you decide whether to buy now or wait.
For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our roundups of the best Mac deals, AirPods deals, and Apple Watch deals.

title: Apple Announces 2026 App Store Award Finalists
content:
Apple today revealed the 45 finalists for its 2026 App Store Awards, with nominations spanning its devices, Apple Arcade, and the Cultural Impact category.


"ElevenReader," "(Not Boring) Camera," and "Raylie" are in contention for iPhone App of the Year. On the Mac, the app nominees are clipboard manager "Paste," task manager "Things 3," and writing app "Ulysses," while "Big Walk," "Blue Prince," and "Crimson Desert" are competing for the gaming award. The full list of finalists follows:

iPhone App of the Year


ElevenReader: A text-to-speech app with AI-generated narration.

(Not Boring) Camera: A customizable camera app inspired by vintage cameras.

Raylie: A flight companion that provides personalized guidance during journeys.



iPhone Game of the Year


BALL x PIT: A game that puts a twist on brick-breaking mechanics.

DAVE THE DIVER: An underwater adventure centered on diving and ocean exploration.

Gambonanza: A chess-inspired game that changes the traditional rules.



iPad App of the Year


Cosmos: A visual discovery app for collecting inspiration in mood boards.

Kiddopia: A collection of educational games and activities for young children.

Mockup: A design tool for planning app and website interfaces.



‌iPad‌ Game of the Year


Aniimo: A fantasy adventure featuring creature companions.

Arknights: Endfield: A science-fiction game with combat on a distant moon.

Where Winds Meet: An adventure built around martial arts combat.



Mac App of the Year


Paste: A clipboard manager for keeping track of copied content.

Things 3: A task manager for organizing to-do lists.

Ulysses: A writing app with tools for formatting documents.



Mac Game of the Year


Big Walk: A multiplayer adventure focused on solving puzzles with friends.

Blue Prince: A mystery game set inside an unusual mansion.

Crimson Desert: A fantasy adventure set in a world shaped by war.



‌Apple Arcade‌ Game of the Year


Perchang World: A physics puzzle game about guiding marbles.

PowerWash Simulator: A cleaning simulation that puts players behind a pressure washer.

Pusheen's Place: A cat-themed game featuring Pusheen.



Apple Vision Pro App of the Year


Adobe Premiere: A video editor with a workspace designed for spatial computing.

MLB: A baseball streaming app offering a view behind home plate.

Museas: An art-viewing app that places virtual galleries in users' surroundings.



‌Apple Vision Pro‌ Game of the Year


Cueva de las Manos: A puzzle game built around manipulating light and shadows.

Ping Pong Club: A spatial table tennis game.

Spatial Ops: A first-person combat game that incorporates players' physical surroundings.



Apple Watch App of the Year


Bevel: A fitness app that interprets health data to offer guidance.

Moonlitt: A tracker for moon phases and lunar events.

StressWatch: A health app for monitoring estimated stress levels.



Apple TV App of the Year


Case Solved: The London Files: A murder mystery game featuring logic puzzles and noir themes.

Letterboxd: A movie discovery app featuring recommendations from friends and critics.

Pocket Casts: A podcast player adapted for listening through a television.



Cultural Impact Apps


Brilliant: An educational app covering mathematics and science.

chilli: An app for participating in environmental political campaigns.

Hearing Buddy: A speech transcription app for deaf and hard-of-hearing users.

Karrot: A local marketplace for buying and selling within neighborhoods.

setlog: A social camera app focused on sharing everyday experiences with friends.

Unedo: A Spanish-learning app that uses games and stories.



Cultural Impact Games


and Roger: A narrative game exploring a difficult personal experience.

Consume Me: A game that examines experiences with eating disorders.

PancitoMerge: A game inspired by Mexican food traditions.

Sago Mini Jinja's Garden: A gardening-themed game designed for family play.

Spilled!: An environmental cleanup game set on polluted waters.

Tiny Bookshop: A bookshop game with an emphasis on community.

title: New Apple products coming in 2027: What’s next?
content:
Macworld





What new products will Apple launch in 2027? Rumors point to a redesigned iPhone to mark its 20th anniversary, an OLED iPad Air, and potentially Apple’s first smart glasses. Updated Macs, more affordable iPhones and new AI-focused accessories could also be on the way.
The first launches could arrive in the spring. Reports suggest Apple will introduce the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, potentially alongside an updated iPhone Air. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman also expects new entry-level iPad, iPad Air and iPad Pro models in the first half of 2027.
Later in the year, attention will turn to the iPhone’s anniversary redesign, while camera-equipped AirPods and further smart-home developments could expand Apple’s lineup. 
Below, we round up the latest Apple product rumors for 2027 and beyond, including expected release dates, possible features and whether an upcoming update makes it worth waiting before you buy. Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and in 2027 and beyond.
Apple’s roadmap: At a glance
